name: Arbi Masala with Soy-Tofu Crumble
ingredients: 300 g arbi (taro root), scrubbed and boiled until just tender, peeled and cut into 2 cm pieces
150 g extra-firm tofu, pressed and crumbled
30 g dry soy granules, rehydrated in hot water and squeezed dry
1 tsp (5 ml) mustard or canola oil
½ tsp amchur, or to taste
1 cup chopped spinach or methi leaves
Lemon juice and a modest pinch of salt
steps: Boil the arbi until a knife enters with slight resistance; drain, cool, peel and cut. Avoid overboiling so the pieces hold their shape.
Soak soy granules in boiling water for 8–10 minutes. Drain, rinse once and squeeze firmly. Press and crumble the tofu.
Heat the measured oil in a wide non-stick pan. Add cumin and ajwain; let them sizzle briefly without burning.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander and chilli. Cook until softened, adding a splash of water instead of extra oil if the pan dries.
Stir in soy granules and tofu; cook 4–5 minutes until hot and lightly browned.
Add arbi and fold gently so the pieces remain intact. Cook 5–7 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add spinach or methi and cook until wilted. Finish with amchur, coriander and lemon. Taste before adding more salt.
note: A lighter, higher-protein take on UP-style arbi. Taro is a starchy root, so serve a moderate portion alongside extra non-starchy vegetables; it is not a low-carbohydrate food. Vegan. Nutrition is an approximate calculation and depends on tofu and soy brands.
